content:
**Diagnosis:** the Deployment's `spec.selector.matchLabels` requires `version: v2`, but the pod template only carries `app: myapp` and `env: prod`. Since dev has no `version` label and the selector is the immutable field (adding the label to the template instead would drift prod's pod labels away from dev for no reason), the fix is to drop `version: v2` from the selector. The Service's selector (`app`/`env`) remains a subset of the template labels, so it still matches.

`prod/app.yaml`

```yaml
# SEED REPO: bare prod/app.yaml with a seeded defect.
#
# Application workload, same shape as golden-base/knr-ops/infra/app/deployment.yaml.
# Named myapp-prod (not myapp) for the same reason as dev/app.yaml: no
# namePrefix mechanism here, so env-qualified names are hand-written.
#
# eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn below is left as a documented placeholder: IRSA
# needs the *runtime* ARN of the Role in iam.yaml, which ACK only knows once
# it has actually created that Role (status.ackResourceMetadata.arn) - it
# can't be known at manifest-authoring time. A rendering pipeline (or a
# two-phase apply: create the Role, read its status, patch the ServiceAccount)
# would close this gap; bare's plain kubectl apply has no such step, so this
# ServiceAccount's role-arn has to be patched in by hand after the Role
# exists. See golden-base/bare/README.md.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: myapp-prod
  namespace: app
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: "<REPLACE_WITH_myapp-prod-service-role_ARN_AFTER_CREATE>"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp-prod
  namespace: app
  labels:
    app: myapp
    env: prod
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
      env: prod
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: myapp
        env: prod
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: myapp-prod
      containers:
        - name: myapp
          image: docker.io/myapp/myapp:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 256Mi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: myapp-prod
  namespace: app
spec:
  selector:
    app: myapp
    env: prod
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
  type: ClusterIP
```

Note: if a `myapp-prod` Deployment already exists in the cluster with a different selector, `spec.selector` is immutable on `apps/v1` Deployments — you'd need to delete the existing Deployment (`kubectl delete deploy myapp-prod -n app`) before re-applying. Since the seeded object was rejected at admission, it never got created, so a plain `kubectl apply -f prod/app.yaml` should succeed here.
